items.title: 68189_Al Hall oral history interview
items.q: Dick Vance was the leader with Eddy Barefield, Taft Jordan, I think. We had a good band.

ctx.x: Well, then, tell it the way you want to tell it.

Her father gave her $1500 for a birthday present and this is circa 52nd Street, and she says, my dad gave me $1500 for a birthday present and I want to start a record company and I want you to handle it but I don't want to be known as the sponsor of that, and that's how it came about. So, I got Ben Webster and Jimmy Jones; am I leaving out somebody? Dick Vance. Well, originally it was Bill Coleman but he had already gone to Paris. He did return on a visit and made a

Wax record. But I wasn't the bass player on that, John Levy, was because when we made our first Wax Record, and we got mention for three out of four sides, this was the borderline between swing and bop. This was the last of that sort of thing and Mike Levine gave me a nice writeup in Downbeat.
